Loss definitions by method

Deep ensemble (DE)BDKNFunctional repulsion (FRDE)Weight repulsion (WRDE)First-order repulsion (FoRDE, 1D)Gaussian process (GP)Deep kernel learning (DKL)LDBLLVBLL

Deep ensemble (DE)

\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DE}}=\sum_{i=1}^{H}\frac{1}{2B}\sum_{b=1}^{B}\left[\log\!\left(2\pi v_i(\widetilde x_{ib})\right)+\frac{(y_{ib}-\mu_i(\widetilde x_{ib}))^2}{v_i(\widetilde x_{ib})}\right]
H,\ BNumber of networks and batch size.
\widetilde x_{ib},y_{ib}Preprocessed input and target in network i’s batch.
\mu_i,\ v_iNetwork i’s predicted mean and observation variance.

BDKN

\mathcal L_1=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DE}},\qquad \Phi_{ni}=\mu_i(\widetilde x_n)
\Lambda_0=\sigma_p^{-2}I,\quad\Lambda_n=\Phi^\top\Phi+\Lambda_0,\quad m_n=\Lambda_n^{-1}\Phi^\top y
\alpha_n=\alpha_0+\frac n2,\qquad\beta_n=\beta_0+\frac12\left(\lVert y-\Phi m_n\rVert^2+\sigma_p^{-2}\lVert m_n\rVert^2\right)
\mathcal L_2=-\log\Gamma(\alpha_n)+\alpha_n\log\beta_n-\frac12(\log|\Lambda_0|-\log|\Lambda_n|)+\frac n2\log(2\pi)
\Phi,\ n,\ yFrozen ensemble feature matrix, training count, and target vector.
\sigma_p^2Prior weight variance learned in stage two.
\Lambda_0,\Lambda_n,m_nPrior precision, posterior precision, and posterior mean.
\alpha_0,\beta_0;\ \alpha_n,\beta_nInverse-gamma prior and posterior parameters; prior-only constants omitted from the plotted loss.

Functional repulsion (FRDE)

\mathcal L_1=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DE}}+\lambda R_{\mathrm F},\qquad z_i=(\mu_i(\widetilde s_b))_{b=1}^{P}
d_{ij}=\lVert z_i-\operatorname{sg}(z_j)\rVert^2,\quad h=\operatorname{sg}\!\left(\max\left\{\frac{\operatorname{med}_{i,j}d_{ij}}{\log(H+1)},\varepsilon_h\right\}\right)
R_{\mathrm F}=\sum_{i=1}^{H}\log\left[\sum_{j=1}^{H}\exp(-d_{ij}/h)\right]
z_i,\widetilde s_b, PMean predictions, shared preprocessed repulsion inputs, and their count.
R_{\mathrm F},\lambdaUnweighted functional repulsion and its objective weight.
\mathcal L_2BDKN stage-two loss above, using the trained FRDE features.

Weight repulsion (WRDE)

\mathcal L_1=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DE}}+\lambda R_{\mathrm W},\qquad z_i=\theta_i
d_{ij}=\lVert\theta_i-\operatorname{sg}(\theta_j)\rVert^2,\quad h=\operatorname{sg}\!\left(\max\left\{\frac{\operatorname{med}_{i,j}d_{ij}}{\log(H+1)},\varepsilon_h\right\}\right)
R_{\mathrm W}=\sum_{i=1}^{H}\log\left[\sum_{j=1}^{H}\exp(-d_{ij}/h)\right]
\theta_iAll trainable parameters of network i, including both output heads.
R_{\mathrm W},\lambdaUnweighted weight repulsion and its objective weight.
\mathcal L_2BDKN stage-two loss above, using the trained WRDE features.

First-order repulsion (FoRDE, 1D)

\mathcal L_1=\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DE}}+\lambda R_{\mathrm G},\quad g_i=\left(\frac{\partial\mu_i(\widetilde s_b)}{\partial\widetilde s_b}\right)_{b=1}^{P},\quad z_i=\frac{g_i}{\sqrt{\lVert g_i\rVert^2+\varepsilon_g}}
d_{ij}=\lVert z_i-\operatorname{sg}(z_j)\rVert^2,\quad h_j=\operatorname{sg}\!\left(\max\left\{\frac{\operatorname{med}_{i}d_{ij}}{\log H},\varepsilon_h\right\}\right)
R_{\mathrm G}=\sum_{i=1}^{H}\log\left[\sum_{j=1}^{H}\exp(-d_{ij}/h_j)\right]
g_i,z_iInput-gradient vector on the selected repulsion inputs and its normalized particle.
h_jBandwidth for reference network j.
R_{\mathrm G},\lambdaUnweighted first-order repulsion and its objective weight.
\mathcal L_2BDKN stage-two loss above, using the trained FoRDE features.

Gaussian process (GP)

\mathcal L_{\mathrm{GP}}=\frac{r^\top K_y^{-1}r+\log|K_y|+n\log(2\pi)}{2n},\quad r=y-m(X),\quad K_y=K(X,X)+\sigma^2I
K,m,\sigma^2Configured linear-plus-RBF covariance, mean function, and observation noise variance.
X,y,nPreprocessed training inputs, targets, and training count.

Deep kernel learning (DKL)

\mathcal L_{\mathrm{DKL}}=\frac{r^\top K_{y,\psi}^{-1}r+\log|K_{y,\psi}|+n\log(2\pi)}{2n},\quad K_{y,\psi}=K^{\mathrm{SKI}}(f_\psi(X),f_\psi(X))+\sigma^2I
f_\psi,K^{\mathrm{SKI}}Learned neural features and the configured grid-interpolated RBF covariance.
r,m,\sigma^2Residual y − m(X), mean function, and observation noise variance.

LDBLL

\mathcal L_{\mathrm{LDBLL}}=-\frac1n\log p(y\mid\Phi)+\frac cn\underset{x\in\mathcal I}{\operatorname{mean}}\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left[p(\partial_x f\mid x)\,\Vert\,q(\partial_x f\mid x)\right]
\Phi,nLearned Bayesian linear-layer features and training count.
p(y\mid\Phi)Gaussian Bayesian linear-layer marginal likelihood; its negative per observation is the likelihood curve.
p(\partial_x f\mid x),q(\partial_x f\mid x)Derivative prior and posterior defining the KL penalty.
c,\mathcal IDerivative scaling factor and index points (perturbed training inputs).

VBLL

\mathcal L_{\mathrm{VBLL}}=-\frac1B\sum_{b=1}^{B}\mathbb E_{q(w)}\log\mathcal N(y_b;w^\top\phi_b,\sigma^2)+\frac1n\left[D_{\mathrm{KL}}(q(w)\Vert p(w))-\Omega(\sigma^{-2})\right]
\Omega(\tau)=a\log\tau-\frac{s}{2}\tau
\phi_b,q(w),p(w)Neural features, Gaussian variational last-layer posterior, and Gaussian weight prior.
\sigma^2,\tauLearned observation variance and precision.
a,sConfigured noise-prior degrees-of-freedom coefficient and Wishart scale.
B,nBatch size and training count; regularization weight is 1/n.

Shared repulsion symbols

d_{ij},h,\operatorname{med}Squared particle distance, bandwidth, and median; pairs include i = j.
P,\widetilde s_bRepulsion count and input: B training points, B random domain points, or their 2B-point union.
\operatorname{sg}Stop-gradient: treated as fixed during differentiation.
\varepsilon_h=10^{-6},\ \varepsilon_g=10^{-8}Bandwidth floor and gradient normalization constant.
R_{\mathrm F},R_{\mathrm W},R_{\mathrm G}Separate repulsion panels show R; objective panels show the full loss including λR.
